agree.reason: Accepting the staff's numbers and asking for alternatives is the right approach for commissioners who trust their staff, but the draft never shows that a three-fish limit or a separate for-hire limit would still rebuild the stock, so a resisting commissioner has little reason to change their vote.

honest.reason: It drops the false claim that every boat will close, but 'multiply that across 11 boats' applies one captain's 2016 loss to the whole harbor, 'never got all the way back' goes beyond the two-year figure, and the tackle-shop, fuel-dock and restaurant effects are not in the facts.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 2016 loss as nearly one trip in five and about $27,000, but it leaves the survey at 41 of 70 instead of nearly 60%, and it doesn't show that the cut lands on a small share of the catch while a large share of one boat's income is at stake.

right_comparison.reason: It honestly reports the partial recovery to 155 trips, but it sets the 9% charter share against the 80% private share as if the bag limit fell only on charters, when it applies to all anglers.

qualification.reason: The commission gets nothing it can check: the captain's offer of trip logs from 2016 on and the association's offer to test a catch-reporting app are left out, and the yearly-review idea has no date or trigger attached.

objections.reason: It deals with the trust-the-staff objection by accepting the stock numbers, but it doesn't answer 'you recovered last time' or 'will the alternative meet the target', and it proposes a for-hire limit and annual review the captain never agreed to while leaving out the shorter season he did accept.

fit.reason: At about 340 words it fits a two-minute public comment and is well paced for speaking aloud, though it leaves [NAME] and [HARBOR] as placeholders even though the captain's name is known.
